title: Why Am I Not Finding Wholesale Deals? 7 Honest Reasons (And How to Fix Them)
excerpt: If you're putting in the hours but still not finding wholesale deals, the problem is usually one of a handful of fixable mistakes. Here's an honest breakdown of what's going wrong and exactly how to turn it around.

sections.content: You've watched the videos, read the guides, maybe even sent out a few letters. But the deals aren't coming. Sound familiar? You're not alone. Most new wholesalers go weeks or even months without closing a single deal, not because the market is too competitive, but because of a few specific, correctable mistakes. If you've been asking yourself 'why am I not finding wholesale deals,' this article will give you honest, practical answers.
Reason #1: You're Marketing to the Wrong Lists

One of the biggest mistakes beginners make is blasting generic direct mail or cold calls to huge, unfiltered lists. Sending 1,000 postcards to random homeowners is expensive and ineffective. The investors who find deals consistently are marketing to highly targeted lists of motivated sellers. Think: pre-foreclosures, tax-delinquent properties, absentee owners with high equity, probate leads, and vacant properties. The more specific your list, the better your response rate. A targeted list of 200 motivated sellers will almost always outperform a generic list of 2,000 random homeowners.

Start with one list type and master it before layering in others. Tax-delinquent homeowners with 40%+ equity are often a great starting point because their financial stress is publicly documented and their motivation is clear.
Reason #2: You're Not Making Enough Offers

Wholesaling is a numbers game, and most beginners dramatically underestimate how many offers it takes to land a deal. Industry veterans often say you should expect to make 15 to 30 offers for every one deal you close. If you've made 5 offers this month and none worked out, that's not failure — that's just the pipeline filling up. Commit to making a set number of offers every week and track them in a spreadsheet. Consistency here is everything.
'The investors who close deals aren't smarter than you — they're just making more offers, more consistently, to more targeted sellers.' — Common wisdom among veteran wholesalers
Reason #3: Your Numbers Are Off

If your offers keep getting rejected by sellers or ignored by buyers, your math might be the problem. The core formula in wholesaling is: Maximum Allowable Offer (MAO) = ARV × 70% − Repair Costs − Your Wholesale Fee. If you're using an inaccurate After Repair Value (ARV), every number downstream gets skewed. Overestimate the ARV and you'll overpay for deals your cash buyers won't touch. Underestimate it and you'll lose deals you could have closed. Use a reliable tool like the free [Deal Calculator at AIWholesail](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to run your numbers accurately before making any offer.
A Quick Example

Let's say a property has an ARV of $250,000 and needs $40,000 in repairs. Using the 70% rule: $250,000 × 0.70 = $175,000, minus $40,000 in repairs = $135,000 max offer. If you want a $15,000 wholesale fee, your offer to the seller should be no more than $120,000. If you're offering $145,000 on that same deal, no cash buyer will pay you a spread — and you'll wonder why nothing is working.
Reason #4: You Don't Have a Real Buyer's List

Finding a motivated seller is only half the equation. If you don't have cash buyers ready to close, even the best deal will fall apart. Many beginners focus 100% of their energy on finding sellers and zero on building their buyer network. Attend local real estate investor meetups, join Facebook groups for cash buyers in your market, and reach out to investors who are actively buying. In competitive markets like [Atlanta](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/atlanta-ga), [Dallas](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/dallas-tx), and [Phoenix](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/phoenix-az), having 10 to 20 verified cash buyers in your database before you find a deal puts you in a much stronger position.

items: Attend your local REIA (Real Estate Investors Association) meetings monthly
Post in local Facebook groups for real estate investors asking for active cash buyers
Connect with hard money lenders who can refer you to their borrower networks
Build relationships with other wholesalers who may co-wholesale deals with you
Use Craigslist or BiggerPockets to find investors actively buying in your zip codes

sections.content: Reason #5: You're Only Using One Marketing Channel

Relying on a single strategy — say, driving for dollars or cold calling alone — limits your deal flow significantly. The most successful wholesalers stack multiple marketing channels at the same time. Direct mail, cold calling, SMS marketing, bandit signs, Google Pay-Per-Click ads, and social media outreach all serve different seller segments. When you layer two or three of these together, your chances of catching a motivated seller at the right moment multiply fast. Start with the one that fits your budget and time, then add a second channel once you've dialed in the first.
Reason #6: You're Giving Up Too Early in the Follow-Up Cycle

Most deals don't come from the first contact. Studies of direct mail campaigns show that response rates on the 4th or 5th touchpoint are often higher than the first. A seller who ignores your letter in January may call you in April when their situation has changed. Set up a follow-up system — whether it's a CRM, a simple spreadsheet, or an automated text sequence — and stay in front of your leads for 6 to 12 months. Wholesalers who quit after one or two contacts are leaving money on the table.

Set a rule: no lead gets removed from your follow-up list until they've been contacted at least 5 times across 3 or more months. Many seasoned wholesalers get deals from leads they first contacted 8 to 12 months earlier.
Reason #7: You Haven't Learned the Fundamentals Yet

This one is hard to hear, but it's important. Many people dive into wholesaling without a solid foundation in how the process actually works — from finding leads and running comps to building contracts and closing with a title company. If you're still fuzzy on the basics, deals will slip through your hands even when opportunity is right in front of you. Take the time to get solid on the fundamentals before spending money on marketing. Check out the [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) for a step-by-step walkthrough of the full process, and the broader [Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) if you're still building your overall investing knowledge base.
The Bottom Line: Wholesale Deals Don't Find You

If you're not finding deals, it almost always comes back to one of these seven issues: the wrong lists, too few offers, bad math, no buyer network, single-channel marketing, weak follow-up, or gaps in your knowledge. The good news is that every single one of these is fixable. Pick the one that resonates most with your current situation and spend the next 30 days fixing it specifically. Small, focused improvements compound quickly in wholesaling.
